evidence.locator: interview question: heart of Beyond's story
evidence.paraphrase: Jung describes questioning the Federation's aspirational ideals while developing friendships among the ensemble.
Jung says the role's name Ben was used in the script, but not spoken in the film.
Jung says that at interview time he had not seen the final fully rendered version, although he had viewed temporary versions.

evidence.locator: fan questions about Lily and Picard scenes and editing
evidence.paraphrase: Frakes recalls that the script's variety of tones aided the Lily-Picard relationship and that editors did not consider removing their scenes.
Frakes recalls pitching Q for the films and explicitly qualifies his recollection of the studio's alleged objection.
Frakes recalls a budget-driven change in music licensing and credits Peter Lauritson with locating a more affordable selection.
Berman recalls a darker initial premise from Piller and describes later revisions and interventions that changed its tone.
Stillwell says he coordinated multiple script drafts, attributes overall authorship to Piller, and assisted with a completed but unpublished behind-the-scenes book.

source_account_summaries.text: In a studio-hosted interview, co-writer Doug Jung explains how his work on Beyond aimed to examine the Federation's vision while bringing crew relationships into focus. He also describes a script-only character name and notes that he had yet to see a final rendered cut when interviewed. These are claims about development and his viewing status, not a reading of the finished film.

Director Jonathan Frakes revisits choices made for First Contact: maintaining an interpersonal arc amid different genres, preserving those scenes in the edit, seeking a different recurring antagonist, and adjusting music choices to financial constraints. His recollections invite comparison with production records but do not substitute for them.

Two studio-published interviews offer different vantage points on Insurrection's writing process. Producer Rick Berman describes an early, considerably bleaker story that evolved through substantial input. Script coordinator Eric Stillwell recalls managing multiple revisions and helping Michael Piller with a completed but unpublished book about its creation. Their accounts document remembered process, not independently inspected drafts or the book manuscript.
